one_liner: Header-only base-10 int32/int64 to/from-string conversion; beats stringstream, to_string, atoi/strtol, stoi.
what_it_does: Two free functions, to_chars and from_chars, convert 32/64-bit signed and unsigned integers to and from base-10 decimal text in a caller-supplied buffer. The result types mirror the ptr/ec shape of C++17 std::to_chars/std::from_chars but are rigtorp's own structs, so calling code isn't identical to the standard API. No floating point, no non-decimal bases, no allocation.
how_it_is_fast: to_chars precomputes the exact digit count with a clz-based bit-length-to-decimal-digits formula (__builtin_clz/__builtin_clzll against a static power-of-10 table) so it writes straight into a correctly sized span instead of a scratch buffer plus reversal or a strlen pass, then emits digits back-to-front via repeated /10, %10. from_chars accumulates digits with __builtin_mul_overflow/__builtin_add_overflow so overflow detection adds no separate check pass; a from_chars_unchecked variant skips overflow checks for a further speedup. Everything is noexcept, constexpr, and hinted with __builtin_expect.
when_to_use: Hot loops converting many 1-9 digit signed/unsigned 32/64-bit integers to base-10 text (log lines, CSV/JSON emitters, wire protocols).
Parsing base-10 integers with overflow detection but without exceptions or locale overhead (from_chars).
Trusted, pre-validated input where the unchecked from_chars_unchecked path's extra speed is worth skipping validation.
You already have a fixed buffer/pointer and want to skip std::to_string's allocation or stringstream's formatting machinery.
GCC/Clang-only target where vendoring one ~200-line, zero-dependency header is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Need floating-point to_chars/from_chars — not implemented at all here.
Need MSVC support — code depends on GCC/Clang builtins (__builtin_clz, __builtin_clzll, __builtin_mul_overflow, __builtin_add_overflow) with no MSVC equivalents provided.
Need real interchangeability with std::to_chars/std::from_chars (exact result types, base 2-36, std::chars_format) — this API is similar but distinct, not a swap-in.

Want the fastest available integer formatter — sibling libraries (jeaiii/itoa, c4core) use digit-pair lookup tables and report larger margins; this repo never benchmarks against them or against actual std::to_chars.
Expect upstream maintenance — no commits, issues, or PRs since the 2023-09-25 push; algorithm and code are unchanged since the 2018 copyright.

integration.dependencies: none for consumers (vendors Google Benchmark and Catch2 only for the repo's own benchmark/test binaries)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (if constexpr); relies on GCC/Clang builtins, exact minimum GCC/Clang version not documented
integration.platforms: any GCC/Clang target (x86-64, aarch64, etc.); MSVC not supported, no intrinsic fallback provided
integration.thread_safety: not documented; code has no shared mutable state (only const power-of-10 tables), so functions appear reentrant
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same ptr/ec result shape as std::to_chars/from_chars per README but with distinct result struct types, and a buffer-based, non-allocating signature that doesn't match stringstream/to_string/atoi/strtol/stoi at all

gotchas: from_chars_unchecked skips overflow validation entirely — only safe on pre-validated input.
to_chars_result/from_chars_result are rigtorp's own types, not std::to_chars_result/std::from_chars_result — don't assume interchangeability.
Caller must size the output buffer itself (worst case 11 bytes for int32/uint32 with sign, 20 for int64/uint64); no allocating convenience wrapper is provided.
Compiler-builtin dependent (__builtin_clz/__builtin_mul_overflow/etc.) — porting off GCC/Clang requires substituting equivalents.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over Boost.Charconv or c4core when you want a zero-dependency, ~200-line header covering only base-10 32/64-bit integers and don't need float support; pick Boost.Charconv or c4core instead when you need floats or an actual std::to_chars/from_chars head-to-head, since this repo never benchmarks against std at all.
verified_claims_summary: In-repo Google Benchmark dated 2017-12-26 on a Xeon E5-2620 v4 (compiler/flags not disclosed): to_chars ran 9-20ns vs sprintf 73-87ns, std::to_string 76-90ns, and std::stringstream 34-55ns; checked from_chars ran 9-19ns vs atoi/strtol 14-28ns and std::stoi 16-29ns; from_chars_unchecked ran 4-10ns. No std::to_chars/std::from_chars comparison exists in the repo.
